\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{താഴ്ത്തുക} (tāḻttuka)}{താഴ്ത്തുക (tāḻttuka)}]{\ml{താഴ്ത്തുക} (tāḻttuka) — to lower}

\label{lesson:ML-C450-talttuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to go higher, then the Malayalam for to lift up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{താഴ്ത്തുക}}
\textbf{\ml{താഴ്ത്തുക}} — \emph{tāḻttuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to lower\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{കടക്കാരൻ} \ml{സാധനങ്ങളുടെ} \ml{വില} \ml{താഴ്ത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭakkāran sādhanaṅṅaḷuṭe vila tāḻtti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper lowered the prices of the goods.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{താഴ്ത്തി}, \emph{tāḻtti}.

The causative of \ml{താഴുക}, to sink; \ml{താഴെ}, below, is the same root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{താഴ്ത്തുക}} (\emph{tāḻttuka}) is native Dravidian, the causative of \ml{താഴുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to sink, to come low\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3178), the root of \ml{താഴെ}, \textquotedblleft{}below\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tāḻttuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tāḻttuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭakkāran sādhanaṅṅaḷuṭe vila tāḻtti.} — The shopkeeper lowered the prices of the goods.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to go higher, then the Malayalam for to lift up, then say \emph{tāḻttuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{താഴ്ത്തുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To lower\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഉറപ്പാക്കുക} (uṟappākkuka)}{ഉറപ്പാക്കുക (uṟappākkuka)}]{\ml{ഉറപ്പാക്കുക} (uṟappākkuka) — to ensure; to make sure}

\label{lesson:ML-C450-urappakkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to lift up, then the Malayalam for to lower.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഉറപ്പാക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറപ്പാക്കുക}} — \emph{uṟappākkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to ensure; to make sure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{എല്ലാ} \ml{കുട്ടികൾക്കും} \ml{ഭക്ഷണം} \ml{കിട്ടി} \ml{എന്ന്} \ml{അധ്യാപകൻ} \ml{ഉറപ്പാക്കി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ellā kuṭṭikaḷkkuṁ bhakṣaṇaṁ kiṭṭi ennŭ adhyāpakan uṟappākki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The teacher made sure that all the children got food.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഉറപ്പാക്കി}, \emph{uṟappākki}.

Built on \ml{ഉറപ്പ്}, firmness, certainty.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറപ്പാക്കുക}} (\emph{uṟappākkuka}) is a native Malayalam compound: \ml{ഉറപ്പ്}, \textquotedblleft{}firmness, assurance\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 721), and \ml{ആക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 333): to make a thing firm.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟappākkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟappākkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ellā kuṭṭikaḷkkuṁ bhakṣaṇaṁ kiṭṭi ennŭ adhyāpakan uṟappākki.} — The teacher made sure that all the children got food.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to lift up, then the Malayalam for to lower, then say \emph{uṟappākkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{സംരക്ഷിക്കുക} (saṁrakṣikkuka)}{സംരക്ഷിക്കുക (saṁrakṣikkuka)}]{\ml{സംരക്ഷിക്കുക} (saṁrakṣikkuka) — to protect; to preserve}

\label{lesson:ML-C450-samraksikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to lower, then the Malayalam for to ensure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സംരക്ഷിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{സംരക്ഷിക്കുക}} — \emph{saṁrakṣikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to protect; to preserve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{നാട്ടുകാർ} \ml{ആ} \ml{പഴയ} \ml{കുളം} \ml{സംരക്ഷിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāṭṭukār ā paḻaya kuḷaṁ saṁrakṣiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The local people preserved that old pond.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{സംരക്ഷിച്ചു}, \emph{saṁrakṣiccu}.

The noun is \ml{സംരക്ഷണം}, protection.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{സംരക്ഷിക്കുക}} (\emph{saṁrakṣikkuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{saṁrakṣaṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}guarding, preservation, protection\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṁrakṣikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saṁrakṣikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāṭṭukār ā paḻaya kuḷaṁ saṁrakṣiccu.} — The local people preserved that old pond.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to lower, then the Malayalam for to ensure, then say \emph{saṁrakṣikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{സംരക്ഷിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To protect; to preserve\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തുക} (meccappeṭuttuka)}{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തുക (meccappeṭuttuka)}]{\ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തുക} (meccappeṭuttuka) — to improve}

\label{lesson:ML-C450-meccappetuttuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to ensure, then the Malayalam for to protect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തുക}}
\textbf{\ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തുക}} — \emph{meccappeṭuttuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to improve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവൾ} \ml{തന്റെ} \ml{ഇംഗ്ലീഷ്} \ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaḷ tanṟe iṁglīṣŭ meccappeṭutti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She improved her English.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തി}, \emph{meccappeṭutti}.

The intransitive is \ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുക}, to get better.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തുക}} (\emph{meccappeṭuttuka}) is built on \ml{മെച്ചം}, \textquotedblleft{}an advantage, the better of a thing\textquotedblright{}, which DEDR 4841 lists as Malayalam \emph{meccam}, \textquotedblleft{}excellency, superiority\textquotedblright{}, in an article on height and the top of things; -\ml{പ്പെടുത്തുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to cause to be\textquotedblright{}, comes from native \ml{പെടുക} (DEDR 3853).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{meccappeṭuttuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{meccappeṭuttuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaḷ tanṟe iṁglīṣŭ meccappeṭutti.} — She improved her English.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to ensure, then the Malayalam for to protect, then say \emph{meccappeṭuttuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മെച്ചപ്പെടുത്തുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To improve\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അവസാനിപ്പിക്കുക} (avasānippikkuka)}{അവസാനിപ്പിക്കുക (avasānippikkuka)}]{\ml{അവസാനിപ്പിക്കുക} (avasānippikkuka) — to wrap up; to end}

\label{lesson:ML-C450-avasanippikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to protect, then the Malayalam for to improve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അവസാനിപ്പിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{അവസാനിപ്പിക്കുക}} — \emph{avasānippikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to wrap up; to end\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{രണ്ട്} \ml{മണിക്കൂറിന്} \ml{ശേഷം} \ml{അവർ} \ml{ചർച്ച} \ml{അവസാനിപ്പിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raṇṭŭ maṇikkūṟinŭ śēṣaṁ avar carcca avasānippiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After two hours they ended the discussion.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{അവസാനിപ്പിച്ചു}, \emph{avasānippiccu}.

The intransitive is \ml{അവസാനിക്കുക}, to come to an end.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{അവസാനിപ്പിക്കുക}} (\emph{avasānippikkuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{avasāna}, \textquotedblleft{}a stopping-place; the end\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 860), with the Malayalam causative verb ending -\ml{ിപ്പിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avasānippikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avasānippikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raṇṭŭ maṇikkūṟinŭ śēṣaṁ avar carcca avasānippiccu.} — After two hours they ended the discussion.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to protect, then the Malayalam for to improve, then say \emph{avasānippikkuka} again
\end{itemize}
